newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Rebel leader named Number Two in S.Leone junta.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader named Number Two in S.Leone junta.

text.p: Sierra Leone's rebel leader Foday Sankoh, in prison in Nigeria, was named on Tuesday as number two in the military junta that seized power in Freetown six weeks ago, state radio said.
It said the appointment was made by junta leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah, who formally declared himself head of state, with Sankoh as his deputy.

The radio said Koromah also announced a large cabinet drawn from a cross section of the West African country and with former deputy military ruler Captain Solomon Musa as chief secretary. Details of other appointments were not available.
The coup leaders have been isolated internationally since they toppled the elected government of president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on May 25.
The United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity, as well as several governments, condemned the coup and demanded the reinstatement of Kabbah, who fled to neighbouring Guinea.
Regional superpower Nigeria tried to reverse the coup militarily on June 2 but the poorly orchestrated effort was frustrated by Koromah's soldiers and Sankoh's guerrillas allied to the coup leaders.
Tuesday's cabinet announcement appeared timed by Koromah to drive home the fact that he was still in charge, following a clandestine radio broadcast by Kabbah earlier on Tuesday.

The ousted leader, broadcasting on the FM frequency in the capital from a radio identifying itself as "the True Voice of Sierra Leone" called on soldiers and rebels to defect to a Nigerian-led regional force.

Many ordinary Sierra Leoneans also condemn Koromah's coup, which was followed by widespread violence and looting which forced the country's predominantly Lebanese business community to flee en masse. Shops and businesses remain closed.
Local commentators said Koromah had had difficulty finding credible Sierra Leoneans willing to join his government.
The state radio said Koromah had asked for representatives from various professional bodies in the country to be part of the government.
